Committees of inspection were elected in towns across the colonies, exactly as the agreement asked. They did publish names. Newspapers printed lists of violators, and the pressure worked: British imports to the colonies collapsed in 1775.

Nobody voting in early 1775 knew that. They did not know Lexington and Concord were months away. People made the choice you just made without knowing how it ended, and reasonable neighbors chose differently from one another.
What did you wish you knew before you voted, that nobody in 1775 could have known?
Mr. Hale and Mrs. Porter both thought they were doing the right thing. What was each of them most afraid of?
Was there a choice here with no cost to anyone? What does that tell you about the decisions people faced?
